method: Existing phase driver: one warmup plus nine measured samples, medians, alternating engine order, fresh runtimes/output, exact output parity; phases exclude prior phases. Swe21 benchmarking finished before run. No wall-time CI threshold. Dirty production-sweep working tree, no baseline rebuild.

Temporary dependency-free Rust GlobalAlloc wrapper around System, linked to the same release liblimits. Lex/parse/check/compile outside counters; one unreported warmup per engine/workload; fresh runtime and Vec output each execution. Counts cover execution and runtime destruction, excluding output destruction. Requested bytes are allocator payload sizes, not RSS; sum includes full realloc requests and is not peak memory. Atomics affect timings, so this probe reports no throughput. All outputs assert 2584 or 75025. All three source variants compute the same Fibonacci value; local_scope adds let copy=n; captured_scope adds fn captured(){return n;} per call, so extra statements and closure creation prevent interpreting allocation differences as isolated optimization effects.
source_template: fn fib(n){EXTRA if n<2{return n;}return fib(n-1)+fib(n-2);}print(fib(N));

throughput: No gross regression demonstrated by same-host release control. First 9-sample current fib25 tree/VM medians 443.428/51.917 ms. Five-sample order HEAD,current,current,HEAD measured tree 304.121,312.097,367.601,380.576 ms and VM 32.434,37.916,41.257,40.777 ms. Reverse adjacent pair current/HEAD VM differs by 1.18%; first pair by 16.90%. Large between-run variation and sequential host control prevent attributing smaller differences. Exact output parity asserted throughout. These are runtime phase timings, not end-to-end times.
historical_comparison: Historical codegen-before fib25 tree/VM 262.106/40.412 ms; codegen-after 275.233/34.526 ms; codegen-after-initial 331.154/37.916 ms. Original historical host conditions are not controlled and runtime implementation was evolving during those snapshots per bench/README.md. Current 9-sample run and contemporaneous 5-sample controls demonstrate material host/time variation. Historical snapshot ratios do not prove safety-fix effects or universal performance.
allocations: Frame-only VM fib18 and fib25 each use 30 allocation calls plus 8 realloc calls, around 5.3 KB peak live payload above pre-execution baseline. Source review confirms no per-call heap Scope allocation in frame_only branch. Captured variant fib25 has 729768 allocation calls plus 2819 realloc calls, but peak live requested bytes 185013 vs 182117 at fib18; periodic VM heap collection bounds dead scopes for this workload. After every runtime is dropped, 8 requested bytes remain, belonging to the still-live output Vec; no retained runtime payload observed by this probe. Captured closure semantics legitimately require heap environments, and extra declaration statements make the variants different workloads. No actual resource defect identified.
limitations: Requested allocator payload bytes exclude allocator metadata and RSS; allocation instrumentation uses atomics and gives no throughput measurement. Inputs are Fibonacci and small workflow fixtures, not a universal workload suite. No speed assertions added to CI, no dependencies/core changes/commits/branches.
